records.public_claim_text: Site managers from 19% (134) cultural properties, 14% (10) natural properties, and 36% (4) of mixed properties were aware that there were elements associated with the property that had been inscribed on the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Site managers from 19% (134) cultural properties, 14% (10) natural properties, and 36% (4) of mixed properties were aware that there were elements associated with the property that had been inscribed on the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

records.public_claim_text: Of the 14 properties reporting that their national authorities intended to designate, in whole or in part, the World Heritage property as a UNESCO Global Geopark, the majority (9) are cultural.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Of the 14 properties reporting that their national authorities intended to designate, in whole or in part, the World Heritage property as a UNESCO Global Geopark, the majority (9) are cultural.

records.public_claim_text: Overall, it is noted that there are very few points of direct contact between World Heritage properties and other designations/programmes, with 64% of site managers having no contact with their counterparts responsible for other designations/programmes.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Overall, it is noted that there are very few points of direct contact between World Heritage properties and other designations/programmes, with 64% of site managers having no contact with their counterparts responsible for other designations/programmes.

records.public_claim_text: However, when looking at which objective was most fully achieved, the most successful objective was that of integrating human rights based approaches, with 37% of site managers reported their property fully achieving their objectives.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: However, when looking at which objective was most fully achieved, the most successful objective was that of integrating human rights based approaches, with 37% of site managers reported their property fully achieving their objectives.

records.public_claim_text: Approximately half (49%) of site managers stated that there are no relevant Committee recommendations for them to implement at their properties (this is particularly acute in North America where this reaches 68%).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Approximately half (49%) of site managers stated that there are no relevant Committee recommendations for them to implement at their properties (this is particularly acute in North America where this reaches 68%).

records.public_claim_text: When asked to comment, a significant number of site managers indicated that they were in the process of preparing retrospective SOUVs (as 20 retrospective SOUV are still pending for properties in the Europe sub-regions) or management plans and expected to better identify attributes during this work.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: When asked to comment, a significant number of site managers indicated that they were in the process of preparing retrospective SOUVs (as 20 retrospective SOUV are still pending for properties in the Europe sub-regions) or management plans and expected to better identify attributes during this work.

records.public_claim_text: While the most commonly reported current and potential major negative factor for natural World Heritage properties is climate change and severe weather events, when the more specific sub-factors are considered, invasive/alien terrestrial species was the most commonly reported current and/or potential negative factor for 58% (40 out of 69) of properties.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: While the most commonly reported current and potential major negative factor for natural World Heritage properties is climate change and severe weather events, when the more specific sub-factors are considered, invasive/alien terrestrial species was the most commonly reported current and/or potential negative factor for 58% (40 out of 69) of properties.

records.public_claim_text: The impact of tourism/visitors/recreation was also a significant concern for natural properties: 52% (36) of properties considered this factor as a current negative impact and 54% (37) as a potential negative impact.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The impact of tourism/visitors/recreation was also a significant concern for natural properties: 52% (36) of properties considered this factor as a current negative impact and 54% (37) as a potential negative impact.

records.public_claim_text: Water (rain/water table) is the most commonly cited secondary factor affecting negatively at 34% (160 out of 464) of cultural properties and, is by far the most frequently reported negative factor in Northern Europe at 49% (32 out of 65) and Southern Europe at 40% (71 out of 176).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Water (rain/water table) is the most commonly cited secondary factor affecting negatively at 34% (160 out of 464) of cultural properties and, is by far the most frequently reported negative factor in Northern Europe at 49% (32 out of 65) and Southern Europe at 40% (71 out of 176).

records.public_claim_text: Temperature is impacting negatively at 26% (122 out of 464) of cultural properties, wind at 23% (109), pests at 23% (106) and micro-organisms at 20% (91).
